name: UV disinfection
principle: Published licensor practice (Trojan, Xylem Wedeco): water passes banks of low-pressure or medium-pressure UV lamps (or emerging LED arrays) emitting ~254 nm UV-C that damages microbial DNA/UV-C proteins at a delivered dose of 20-100 mJ/cm2; no chemical residual, no DBPs; reactors sized with validated dose-monitoring and automatic lamp-intensity control.

process_steps.name: UV reactor exposure
equipment: low- or medium-pressure lamp banks (Trojan UVSwift/UltraFlow)

costs.metric: total capital cost, UV disinfection system
costs.basis: Equipment $120,000 + structural $64,000 + electrical $20,000 + miscellaneous $40,000; O&M $19,190/yr (energy $3,300, lamps/chemicals $2,840, cleaning $1,180, maintenance $1,440, process control $6,240, testing $4,160). The sheet does NOT state the design flow, so it cannot be normalised to m3/d; the underlying WERF study covers 1, 10 and 100 mgd with lamps banded 1-5, 5-10 and 19-100 mgd.

source.note: EPA 832-F-99-064, Ultraviolet Disinfection, Tables 3A-3B: USD 244,000 capital, USD 19,190/yr O&M; design flow not stated, read 2026-11-16

costs.metric: capital cost, UV disinfection at plant peak flow
costs.basis: Derived: $3,350,000 for low-pressure high-output UV sized for 42 mgd (158,987 m3/d) = $21.1/m3/d. About half the capital was modifying the outfall into a UV chamber; with an existing chlorine contact tank the report says the cost could fall by up to $1.6M, giving about $11/m3/d. Chlorination/dechlorination for the same flow was $1,150,000.

source.note: NYSERDA-funded Southtowns WWTP study, Table 8-1 (2004 dollars): UV capital $3.35M at 42 mgd peak flow, read 2026-11-16
